summary: This program builds a playlist of Song objects, sorts it by artist, then copies it into a LinkedList to show how to insert a song at a chosen position and remove a song from the middle of the list.

lines.text: LinkedList is the collection this exercise focuses on; it stores each song in a node that points to its neighbours, so inserting or deleting in the middle does not shift every later element.
The playlist starts as an ArrayList declared through the List interface, which is the usual habit so the concrete class can be swapped later without touching the rest of the code.
Each Song carries a title, artist, genre, and energy rating, so the collection holds real objects rather than loose strings.
The enhanced for loop walks the collection in order without you managing an index.
Comparator.comparing with a method reference builds the comparison rule from the artist field, and sort rearranges the list in place using it.
forEach with a method reference is the compact equivalent of the loop above; it hands each song to println.
Passing an existing collection to the constructor copies its elements, so the LinkedList begins with the same four songs in artist order.

lines.text: Naming the position in a variable makes the intent clear and lets the same number be reused in the message printed below.
The two-argument add inserts at the given index instead of appending, and everything from that index onward moves one place later.
remove(int) deletes the element at that index and returns it, so the removed song can be reported rather than silently discarded.
